request: Project managers should be able to see the full history of engagement with a country before starting a new mission.
gaps: What specific data fields are included in the 'full history of engagement'?
What access controls are in place to prevent unauthorized users from viewing sensitive engagement data?
What happens to access permissions when users change roles or leave the organization?
How will the system handle duplicate or inaccurate engagement records?
What measures are in place to ensure data confidentiality during export?

proposals.summary: This release will provide project managers with access to the complete engagement history for each country in the Government CRM, enhancing their ability to prepare for new missions. The feature will include filters for ease of navigation and an export option for offline review.

core_commitments.text: Project managers can view a complete engagement history for any selected country.
The system provides filters to navigate engagement history effectively.

in_scope.text: Enable access to engagement history for all countries tracked in the CRM.
Implement date and type filters (e.g., meetings, communications) for project managers to refine their view of engagement history.
Allow project managers to export the engagement history as a PDF or CSV format.
Display engagement history with details including date, type of engagement, and participants.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not include live updates to engagement histories during ongoing missions.
Real-time collaboration features will not be available in this release.
The release will not provide engagement history for users who do not have project manager roles.
Integration with external data sources for historical engagement data is excluded.

assumptions.text: Project managers will have the required access permissions to view country engagement history.
assumptions.why_implicit: The request assumes that project managers already have defined roles in the CRM with the necessary access.

assumptions.text: Engagement history data is currently stored and can be retrieved from the existing CRM database.
assumptions.why_implicit: The request implies that there is a system in place to track and store engagement history.

assumptions.text: Users will have sufficient training to navigate the new engagement history feature.
assumptions.why_implicit: The request assumes that users are familiar with the CRM's interface and do not require additional training.

definitions.definition: A comprehensive record of all interactions with a specific country, including meetings, communications, dates, participants, and types of engagement.
Users assigned to manage specific projects involving country engagements within the CRM.
A project or initiative related to international engagement that is in the planning or preparation stage.

success_criteria.metric: Percentage of project managers able to successfully access and view the complete engagement history for a country
success_criteria.measurement: User feedback and testing during the release review phase.

C1.challenge: The proposal defines 'full history of engagement' but lacks clarity on which specific data fields are included in this record.
C1.failure_scenario: A project manager attempts to access the engagement history but finds essential data fields missing, leading to incomplete information for mission preparation.
C1.resolution_test: The proposal explicitly lists all the specific fields included in the 'full history of engagement' definition.

history.text: The proposal defines 'full history of engagement' but lacks clarity on which specific data fields are included in this record.

I have revised the definition of 'full history of engagement' to explicitly include specific data fields such as date, type of engagement, participants, and a summary of engagement outcomes. This change clarifies what project managers can expect to see in the engagement history. [changed: D1]

The proposal now explicitly lists all specific data fields included in the 'full history of engagement'. Evidence: "A comprehensive record of all interactions with a specific country, including meetings, communications, dates, participants, types of engagement, and a summary of engagement outcomes."

C2.challenge: The proposal assumes project managers already have the required access permissions without detailing how sensitive engagement records will be protected from unauthorized access.
C2.failure_scenario: A project manager views confidential engagement information that they should not have access to because the permissions are not correctly defined, leaking sensitive diplomatic information to the wrong personnel.
C2.resolution_test: The proposal clearly outlines the access control mechanisms and the specific permissions required for project managers to access engagement history.

history.text: The proposal assumes project managers already have the required access permissions without detailing how sensitive engagement records will be protected from unauthorized access.

I have added details to specify the access control mechanisms, stating that project managers will be granted specific roles that confer permissions based on their project involvement. This ensures that sensitive engagement records are protected appropriately depending on the user's role in the CRM. [changed: A1]

The proposal has added details outlining the access control mechanisms to protect sensitive engagement records. Evidence: "Project managers will be granted specific roles that confer permissions based on their project involvement. This ensures that sensitive engagement records are protected appropriately depending on the user's role in the CRM."

C3.challenge: The proposal assumes users will have sufficient training but does not specify who will be responsible for providing this training or how it will be conducted.
C3.failure_scenario: Project managers are unable to effectively use the new engagement history feature due to a lack of training, leading to reduced satisfaction and utilization of the feature at rollout.
C3.resolution_test: The proposal includes a plan detailing who will conduct training, what resources will be provided, and how user readiness will be evaluated.

history.text: The proposal assumes users will have sufficient training but does not specify who will be responsible for providing this training or how it will be conducted.

I have revised the assumption to include a plan that outlines the responsibility for training, identifying the training coordinator and specifying the resources provided, along with how user readiness will be evaluated. This aims to ensure users are adequately prepared to utilize the new feature effectively. [changed: A3]

The revised assumption now includes a clear plan for training responsibilities and resources. Evidence: "A plan that outlines the responsibility for training, identifying the training coordinator and specifying the resources provided, along with how user readiness will be evaluated."

C4.challenge: The proposal does not address what happens to access permissions when users change roles or leave the organization, which could risk unauthorized access or data exposure.
C4.failure_scenario: A project manager resigns, and without clearly defined processes for revoking permissions, they still access sensitive engagement data, leading to potential leaks or misuse.
C4.resolution_test: The proposal should outline a process for managing user role changes, including how access permissions are updated or revoked.

history.text: The proposal does not address what happens to access permissions when users change roles or leave the organization, which could risk unauthorized access or data exposure.
I added a process for managing user role changes that includes revoking access permissions for users who change roles or leave the organization. [changed: S5]

The proposal now clearly outlines a process for managing changes in user roles and revoking access permissions. Evidence: "Establish a process for revoking access permissions for project managers who change roles or leave the organization."

C5.challenge: The proposal does not specify how the system will handle duplicate or inaccurate engagement records, which could lead to confusion and inaccuracy in mission preparations.
C5.failure_scenario: A project manager relies on engagement history but encounters duplicate records with conflicting information, leading them to make poor decisions based on inaccurate data.
C5.resolution_test: The proposal must define how the system ensures the quality of data in engagement histories, including management of duplicates and data accuracy.

history.text: The proposal does not specify how the system will handle duplicate or inaccurate engagement records, which could lead to confusion and inaccuracy in mission preparations.
I included a definition for how the system will manage duplicate engagement records and ensure data accuracy, focusing on data quality checks and validation processes. [changed: S6]

The proposal specifies measures to manage duplicate records and ensure data accuracy. Evidence: "Implement checks and validations to manage duplicate engagement records and ensure data accuracy within engagement histories."

C6.challenge: The proposal lacks measures to ensure data confidentiality during the export process, risking exposure of sensitive information.
C6.failure_scenario: A project manager exports engagement history records containing sensitive diplomatic information and inadvertently shares them inappropriately, breaching confidentiality protocols.
C6.resolution_test: The proposal should detail security measures in place to protect sensitive data during export, including encryption or access restrictions.

history.text: The proposal lacks measures to ensure data confidentiality during the export process, risking exposure of sensitive information.
I outlined security measures, including data encryption and access restrictions, to protect sensitive information during the export process. [changed: S7]

The proposal has defined security measures to protect sensitive data during export. Evidence: "Introduce security measures for the export process, including data encryption and access restrictions to protect sensitive information."

C7.failure_scenario: A project manager attempts to access engagement history but finds missing fields, leading to incomplete information that affects mission planning.
C7.resolution_test: The proposal must clearly specify all data fields included in the engagement history.

C8.challenge: While measures are in place for exports, the proposal does not clarify specific access controls within the CRM to prevent unauthorized users from viewing sensitive engagement data.
C8.failure_scenario: A non-project manager gains access to engagement history records containing sensitive information due to inadequate access controls, leading to a breach of confidentiality.
C8.resolution_test: The proposal must detail the access controls that prevent unauthorized access to sensitive engagement data.
